_doc: #732 THE ONE DECLARATION of how the Store's controls LOOK. The Store draws three different kinds of control, and before this they were told apart by code alone, so the page-opening entries on the second tab line (Commits, CI-CD, Mesh, Perms) drew as bare text and read as captions rather than as something to tap. Three styles, one per kind of control: `tab` selects a subset of the fleet (line 1, one per declared group), `page` opens another page (line 2: the feeds, Mesh and Perms), `action` does something to one app (Details, Install, Stop, Uninstall, and every other button btn() draws). The Kotlin (StoreControls + StoreCloudFragment.tabButton/paintTabs/btn) maps a style's fields onto a view and names no style token, colour, icon or caption; which control wears which style is this file.
_doc_where: Declared in libs:appstore's own assets, beside appstore-feeds.json and appstore-fleet-actions.json, NOT in aa_cloud-superapp/build.json: this module is built standalone by ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks and hosted by satellite apps, none of which carry the superapp's build.json, and a module that owns a screen owns that screen's data (libs:appstore/build.gradle says the same of the fleet manifest).
_doc_styles: Every field is read by StoreControls.parse. Colours are ARGB hex. `fill`/`fill_active` = background (null = none; on an action the verb's own colour from appstore-fleet-actions.json replaces `fill`), `stroke`/`stroke_active` = a 1dp outline (null = no outline), `text`/`text_active` = caption colour, `radius_dp` = corner radius, `stretch` = share the row's width (weight 1) instead of wrapping the caption, `bold` = bold caption, `chevron` = drawn after the caption ('' = none). `_active` is the selected tab or page; an action has no selected state, so it declares none. The three must stay visibly different: test-store-controls.sh fails if any two share their shape (fill / outline / chevron / stretch / square-or-rounded).

tab._role: selects a subset (line 1): a segmented control, square, stretched, filled when active

page._role: opens a page (line 2): an outlined, rounded chip with an icon and a chevron, wrapping its caption, never filled solid

action._role: acts on one app: a solid block in the verb's own colour, white bold caption, slightly rounded

_doc_wearers: `group_tab_style` is the style every line-1 group tab wears (groups come from the fleet manifest, which says nothing about looks). `action_style` is what btn() draws. `pages` is every line-2 entry by id: a feed's id from appstore-feeds.json (its caption stays THERE, its one declaration, so a feed entry here carries no label) or one of the two pages StoreCloudFragment owns, `mesh` and `perms`, whose captions live here. A line-2 id with no entry here still draws, as a `page` with no icon, so a new feed never vanishes for want of an icon.
_doc_apps_mesh: #733 THE APPS MESH PAGE's own words. One page with two ways in: Store ▸ Apps Mesh (the `mesh` entry above, whose label is the page's caption) and Configs ▸ Watchdog ▸ Mesh ▸ Apps Mesh (aa_cloud-superapp/build.json page `apps-mesh`, which must carry the SAME label — test-apps-mesh.sh holds the two equal). Both hosts draw it with AppsMesh.page; neither has a copy. `member_actions` is what tapping a member offers, in this order, each `id` handled by AppsMesh.act (an id with no handler is not drawn, so a typo cannot ship a dead button). `store` is offered only where the page is hosted by the Store, which is the one host with a row to open. `tools` are the page-level buttons. `gaps` is the missing-membership vocabulary: one entry per GapKind, its heading and the remedy the report prints, with {repo} / {missing} / {seen} / {total} filled from the row.

apps_mesh.exposure: Every member's debug API binds 127.0.0.1 on its own port (libs:devtools debug-ports.json) and wants the fleet Bearer token on everything but /api/system/ping. It is NOT served on this phone's mesh address ({mesh}): from the mesh, ssh to the phone and curl the loopback address there.

NO_PROVIDER.label: not a mesh member: ships no signature-guarded fleet provider, so it serves no debug API and /api/fleet/peers never lists it
NO_PROVIDER.fix: link libs:core (it carries libs:devtools) into {repo}/build.json modules and rebuild

NO_DEBUG_API.label: no debug API answered on 127.0.0.1 — not on its assigned port, nor anywhere in the fleet's debug range
NO_DEBUG_API.fix: provider present but the server never answered after a wake: open the app once (a force-stopped app stays stopped), then Re-probe

NO_PERMISSION.label: CONSTELLATION_DATA not held
NO_PERMISSION.fix: link libs:core into {repo} (core declares and requests the permission); if it already links it, reinstall from our release — a signature permission is granted only to the fleet key

PEER_BLIND.label: cannot see the whole mesh ({seen} of {total}; missing {missing})
PEER_BLIND.fix: rebuild {repo} on libs:devtools from #733 — its manifest now queries every mesh member
